text:
noah: RFC follow-up: long-term plan to gate feature transforms behind a capability registry and roll out per-tenant capability declarations. Intended outcome: clearer service boundaries, easier ownership shifts.
mei: Important to define capability schema now. Need fields: capability_id, allowed_effects, latency_class, billing_dimension, cache_compatibility.
junaid: Concern: retrofitting existing tenants will take time. Propose a rollout that only requires declaration for new tenants initially, then 6-month migration for legacy tenants.
noah: Also thinking about a capability-negotiation shim at runtime for cross-service calls so older services can advertise fallbacks.
infra-bot: infra: capability-registry service scaffold created in staging cluster.
mei: Tests: capability validation + contract-checker in CI. Also add a discovery endpoint for orchestration to query tenant capabilities.
junaid: Edge case: third-party plugins that rely on side-effects. We must mark them as "unsafe-for-cutover" and keep them behind orchestrator toggles.
qa-bot: QA: need end-to-end plan with synthetic tenants that exercise every capability permutation. Will take ~10 testcases.
noah: Action items:
- Mei: capability schema PR (ETA 2d)
- Junaid: migration plan for legacy tenants (ETA 1w)
- Infra: service scaffold + discovery endpoint (ETA 3d)
- QA: synthetic permutations matrix (ETA 5d)
We'll track in the migration epic and revisit in next architecture sync.
mei: one more thing 1 64 : If we can tie capability declarations to billing tiers that would help prioritize migrations.
noah: good call. link with product to get adoption incentives.
